[TASK: 2560x1440 2K QHD 16:9 ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic 6x7 medium-format architectural survey photograph.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render razor-sharp ashlar courses, straight timber sash mullions, and crisp slate roofs.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the carriageway with authentic road surfacing, stone setts, whinstone kerbs, and clean flagstone pavements.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   The central communal oval garden contains mature broadleaf urban specimens:
- **Species Composition**: *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore), *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime), *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), and *Betula pendula* (Silver Birch).
- **Phenology (September 3)**: Full, heavy late-summer canopy volume showing early signs of apical senescence, subtle leaf-margin chlorosis on lime and birch canopies, deep olive-green maturity across sycamore foliage, and manicured perennial turf understorey bounded by shrub borders.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Pin-sharp infinite depth of field (f/11). Zero lens blur, tilt-shift, or depth-of-field falloff across foreground and background.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR LIGHT VECTOR (4500K Late afternoon raking sunlight with warm golden highlights): Sun background upper-left (Azimuth 251.3°, Elevation 21.4°). backlit silhouettes with left rim lighting. shadows project forward toward lower-RIGHT.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Medium format 6x7 architectural survey of Ainslie Place, Edinburgh, designed by James Gillespie Graham in 1822. Sweeping concave neoclassical palace-fronted crescent constructed from pale buff-grey Craigleith sandstone ashlar. Principal storey detailed with continuous V-jointed rustication, semicircular arched doorways, geometric radiating fanlights, and four-panel painted timber storm doors. Upper two storeys executed in smooth droved ashlar stone, demarcated by continuous moulded string courses, projecting classical cornice, and a clean stone blocking course concealing slate mansard roofs and ashlar chimneys with terracotta pots. Rhythmic fenestration grid of plumb twelve-pane and four-pane timber sash-and-case windows set in crisp stone reveals. Deep excavated stone basement wells crossed by oversailing ashlar platts and enclosed by continuous black wrought-iron spearhead railings. Roadway surfaced in dark bitumen bordered by dressed whinstone kerbstones and broad sandstone flagstone pavements. Central oval pleasure gardens bounded by iron railings, containing mature *Acer pseudoplatanus*, *Tilia × europaea*, and *Ulmus glabra* trees exhibiting dense, late-summer olive canopies with early September leaf-margin chlorosis over manicured lawn. Facades display authentic historical coal-soot patination in cornice recesses and rain-washed quartz highlights on upper friezes. Cleaned static architectural composition devoid of vehicles and people.
